  # so consumer CI workflows can read, seal, and commit it for their namespace.
  # DEV ONLY default — override with a long random value in real deployments.
  consumerRegistrationSecret: "dev-consumer-registration-secret-change-me"
  # Authentik (DEV ONLY — override). Secret key must be long/random in real use.
  authentikSecretKey: "dev-authentik-secret-key-change-me-0123456789abcdef0123"
  authentikBootstrapPassword: "admin123"
  authentikBootstrapToken: "dev-bootstrap-token-change-me-0123456789"
  # OIDC client creds for the backend. Set deterministically by the blueprint

  authentikClientId: "fuzefront-oidc-client"

  sendgridApiKey: ""
  # Twilio Verify credentials for SMS MFA. Leave empty to run in mock/inert mode.

  twilioAuthToken: "" # legacy account-token auth; prefer the API key below

  twilioApiKeySecret: "" # preferred: Twilio API Key secret
  twilioVerifyServiceSid: ""
  smsAuthSecret: "dev-sms-secret-change-me"

  authentikMendysDbPassword: ""

# ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzeagent-a2a image (izzywdev/FuzeAgent CI builds/publishes
# it; this chart never builds it) configured, via the mounted values.json, to
# serve exactly one tenant: this repo's `app-shell-platform` role. See
# docs/a2a/README.md (the investigation that produced this exact shape) and
# izzywdev/FuzeAgent's docs/a2a/per-product-pod.md (the canonical recipe — do
# not re-derive it). Deliberately NOT a second A2A server implementation and
# NOT onboarded onto the shared a2a-shared/fuzeagent server: the owner decision
# is one pod per product for blast-radius isolation.
# `a2a:` is serialised VERBATIM into the ConfigMap the server reads
# (A2A_VALUES_FILE) — see templates/a2a.yaml. It mirrors EXACTLY the frozen
# contract interface (izzywdev/FuzeAgent's
# agent-templates/contracts/a2a/v1/schema/values-interface.schema.json),
# additionalProperties:false at every level: no invented keys here. Pure
# deployment mechanics (replicas, resources, scheduling, the git-clone
# sidecar, secret plumbing) deliberately live in the separate `a2aDeploy:`
# block below instead — a key added under `a2a` that the server doesn't
# recognize is a validation failure, not a silently-ignored value.
a2a:
  enabled: false
  image:
    # ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzeagent-a2a is a stale/abandoned image (last pushed
    # 2026-08-24; anonymously pullable but no longer built). The image
    # FuzeAgent's own release.yml actively builds and publishes on every
    # release, and what its own a2a-shared/values-prod.yaml points at, is
    # ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuze-a2a (agent-templates/a2a/Dockerfile). Corrected
    # here 2026-09-02 — gate-a2a's own I1 default + the runtime standard doc
    # still name the old `fuzeagent-a2a` repository (already flagged,
    # FuzeAgent PR #257); a resulting I1 finding against this file is that
    # known staleness, not a new fork.
    repository: ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuze-a2a
    # `latest` is the permitted dev-shape tag (forbidden only in
    # values-prod.yaml, which pins an exact CI-built tag) — matches
    # FuzeAgent's own a2a-shared/values.yaml base shape. A blank tag here
    # previously made gate-a2a report the image as "not fully declared" even
    # though the server is disabled; `latest` keeps the declaration complete
    # and verifiable while still describing the disabled dev default.
    tag: "latest"
    pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  service:
    # MUST be ClusterIP — ingress is Cloudflare-tunnel-only, and `inClusterUrl`
    # below must resolve to exactly this Service.
    type: ClusterIP
    port: 8080
  protocolVersion: "1.0"
  # THE ONE VALUE A PER-PRODUCT POD MUST NOT GET WRONG (per-product-pod.md).
  # Unset would default to the SHARED server's card URL and this pod would be
  # unreachable through its own card despite passing every probe.
  inClusterUrl: ""
  # `auth` is left UNSET (not an empty-valued object) in this disabled base
  # shape on purpose: the frozen interface requires `oidcIssuerUrl` whenever
  # `auth` is present at all, so a present-but-empty block is a gate-a2a C3
  # fatal finding on a file that was never meant to carry a real issuer.
  # Mirrors FuzeAgent's own a2a-shared/values.yaml base shape. values-prod.yaml
  # supplies the real `auth:` block for the enabled deployment.
  # auth:
  #   oidcIssuerUrl: ""
  #   oidcDiscoveryUrl: ""
  #   audience: a2a
  #   callerClaim: repo
  cardSigning:
    keySecretRef: { name: "", key: "" }
    keyId: a2a-v1
  # A per-product pod serves ONE tenant. Exactly one entry, empty by default.
  tenants: []

# Chart-internal A2A deployment mechanics — devops slice, NOT part of the
# frozen contract interface (kept out of `a2a:` above so that block stays
# byte-conformant to the schema the server validates).
a2aDeploy:
  replicas: 1
  # GitOps repo-sync: shallow-clones each enabled tenant's repo at `ref` into
  # A2A_REPOS_DIR/<tenant> so the server can project a card + provision agent
  # sessions from THIS repo's own .fuze/manifest.json + agent-templates/roles/.
  # null = anonymous clone (only correct for a PUBLIC tenant repo).
  reposGitTokenSecretRef: null
  providerApiKeySecretRef: null
  # Optional Anthropic-compatible gateway endpoint. Production points this at
  # FuzeInfra LiteLLM so the pod uses the existing FuzeFront gateway credential
  # instead of requiring a second raw provider key in this namespace.
  providerBaseUrl: ""
  gitImage: alpine/git:latest
  agentProvider: anthropic
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 256Mi
    limits:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
  nodeSelector: {}
  affinity: {}
  tolerations: []

--- deploy/helm/fuzefront/values-prod.yaml ---
# =============================================================================
# Production overlay (Contabo k3s), consumed by the Argo CD `fuzefront` Application.
# Differs from local by: GHCR images, public host + TLS, sealed secret, prod
# Authentik OIDC, Prometheus metrics, pre-created Kafka topics, and node-2
# placement for heavy stateless services.
#
# Node topology (see docs/deployment/CONTABO_DEPLOYMENT.md):
#   node-1 (kubernetes.io/hostname=fuzefront-node-1): control-plane + stateful
#           (FuzeInfra Postgres/Redis/Kafka/Chroma live here on local-path).
#   node-2 (kubernetes.io/hostname=fuzefront-node-2): heavy stateless compute
#           (litellm/chat/billing). Relabel/rename to match the real join.
# All secrets come from the SealedSecret `fuzefront-secrets` — never inline here.
# =============================================================================
global:
  imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  # Default placement: none (let the scheduler spread app pods across both nodes).
  # Heavy stateless services pin to node-2 via their own affinity blocks below.
  scheduling:
    nodeSelector: {}
    affinity: {}
    # Tolerate FuzeInfra's durable-node taint.
    #
    # FuzeInfra is tainting its three durable (control-plane/etcd) nodes
    # `fuzeinfra.io/durable=true:NoSchedule` so that application workloads stop
    # landing on them. Measured there on 2026-09-07: 70 and 57 pods on two of the
    # three, 20,585 container restarts, load average 59, and etcd losing
    # heartbeats on the node that was also the raft leader.
    #
    # FuzeFront is explicitly IN SCOPE for those nodes -- it is platform frontend,
    # not a tenant app -- so it must carry the toleration or it gets pushed onto
    # the autoscaled elastic pool, which is reaped on billing boundaries.
    #
    # THIS WILL NOT LOOK BROKEN IF IT IS MISSING. NoSchedule does not evict, so
    # when the taint lands every FuzeFront pod keeps running exactly as before.
    # It breaks at the NEXT restart or rollout, when those pods can no longer be
    # placed back -- a delayed failure that reads as unrelated to the taint. That
    # is why this has to land BEFORE the taint, not after it.
    #
    # TOLERATION IS NOT PLACEMENT. This only makes the durable nodes *eligible*;
    # the scheduler may still choose elastic. Moving specific backend services
    # deliberately ONTO elastic is a separate concern, expressed per-service via
    # nodeSelector/affinity (see PR #910) -- and note the `fuzefront.scheduling`
    # helper resolves per-service over global, so a service that declares its own
    # `tolerations` REPLACES this list rather than adding to it. A service pinned
    # to elastic simply does not need it.
    #
    # Tracked in izzywdev/FuzeInfra#913; the matching FuzeInfra-side tolerations
    # (longhorn, coredns, ARC controller, Argo CD) landed in izzywdev/FuzeInfra#921.
    tolerations:
      - key: fuzeinfra.io/durable
        operator: Equal
        value: "true"
        effect: NoSchedule

# Prometheus scrape annotations on FuzeFront pods. The FuzeInfra Prometheus
# auto-discovers pods carrying prometheus.io/scrape=true (see Phase E). The
# backend exposes /metrics via prom-client; other pods are annotated for when
# their /metrics lands.
observability:
  metrics:
    enabled: true
    path: /metrics

# Fleet policy: only core infra + frontend services stay on the durable/
# control-plane node pool (vmi3383846/vmi3396106); backend/worker pods for an
# individual product move to the autoscaled `elastic` pool instead. Every
# service below reaches its state (Postgres/Redis/Mongo/Kafka) over the
# network in the `fuzeinfra` namespace, not via a local PVC, so this is a
# plain placement change — mirrors FuzeInfra's
# runners/arc/runner-scale-set-values.yaml pattern. `frontend` below is
# deliberately NOT given this block; it is the one service this policy keeps
# on durable.
.elasticPlacement: &elasticPlacement
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
          - matchExpressions:
              - key: fuzeinfra.io/pool
                operator: In
                values:
                  - elastic
  tolerations:
    - key: fuzeinfra.io/elastic
      operator: Exists
      effect: PreferNoSchedule

backend:
  image:
    repository: ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-backend
    tag: 518b5a6eb689
  replicas: 2
  # Serves GET /api/flags for the host shell. Same CLIENT token as the
  # applications-service, read from the Unleash chart's own sealed Secret.
  featureFlags:
    unleashUrl: "http://fuzefront-unleash.fuzefront.svc.cluster.local:4242/api"
    appName: "fuzefront-host"
    tokenSecretName: "unleash-secrets"
    tokenSecretKey: "UNLEASH_CLIENT_TOKEN"
  <<: *elasticPlacement

frontend:
  image:
    repository: ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-frontend
    tag: 518b5a6eb689
  replicas: 2

# Backend 3-way split. Images built by release.yml; `enabled` flips to true in
# the Phase 3 cutover. tag "" is rewritten by CI's release sed.
securityService:
  enabled: true   # serves /api/auth (local auth + seeded users); OIDC falls back to local
  # Synthetic account for post-prod e2e smoke (POST_PROD_EMAIL/POST_PROD_PASSWORD).
  # Fresh address (absent in prod) so the idempotent seed-admin hook does a clean
  # insert with the sealed FUZEFRONT_ADMIN_PASSWORD. See PR #213 (password reseal).
  adminEmail: admin@fuzefront.com
  # Signup email verification (PR #275) — OFF until the sender is proven.
  # While false the code auto-verifies every new account, i.e. verification is not
  # enforced. That remains the SAFE state until a real SMTP sender is proven
  # end-to-end: email-service is enabled and healthy, but with no SMTP host it
  # falls back in-code to localhost:1025 and silently drops every message.
  #
  # This is no longer guarded by prose alone: the chart FAILS TO RENDER if this is
  # true while emailService.email.smtp.host is empty, because flipping it without a
  # deliverable sender locks out EVERY new signup (created unverified, never
  # mailed). Go-live sequence — deploy/contabo/SEAL_PROD_SECRETS.md:
  #   1. owner seals SMTP_USER + SMTP_PASS
  #   2. set emailService.email.smtp.host below (GitOps)
  #   3. PROVE a real message reaches a real inbox  ← password reset revives here
  #   4. only then flip this to true, in a deploy window
  requireEmailVerification: false
  image:
    repository: ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-security-service
    tag: 518b5a6eb689
  # TEMPORARY MITIGATION: 1 replica.
  # The OIDC social-login state (PKCE verifier) lives in a PROCESS-LOCAL Map —
  # AuthentikIdentityProvider.socialStates / mfaChallenges. With 2 replicas and no
  # session affinity, /social/google/start stores state on pod A while the
  # /api/auth/oidc/callback lands on pod B, which has no idea what that state is —
  # observed live: start on ...66gfh, callback on ...pvhm2 -> authentication_failed.
  # Roughly half of all sign-ins failed this way, independent of every other fix.
  # Same flaw affects MFA challenges and broker codes (so 2FA breaks identically).
  # Pinning to 1 replica removes the split; it costs HA for the auth path, so this
  # is a stopgap. PROPER FIX: externalize that state to Redis (FuzeInfra provisions
  # it — delegate the DB/credentials request via @fuze), then restore replicas: 2.
  replicas: 1
  # Server-brokered Google sign-in (PR #329). "true" = enabled — owner has
  # registered this callback in the Google console. Instant rollback: set to
  # "false" to revert to the legacy Authentik Google source flow (no rebuild).
  googleBrokered: "true"
  # Prod browser-facing Google callback URL (app host, not auth-dev).
  googleRedirectUri: "https://app.fuzefront.com/api/v1/security/social/google/callback"
  # @fuzefront/feature-flags (OpenFeature + Unleash) client — gates
  # fuzefront.identity.root-membership (FF-EPIC-17-S1/S2, default OFF in
  # Unleash) via utils/feature-flags.ts (init) + utils/rootMembershipFlag.ts
  # (read). Same token the standalone Unleash chart already seals into
  # `unleash-secrets` (key UNLEASH_CLIENT_TOKEN) — reused rather than
  # duplicated, mirroring applicationsService/backend above. It is a CLIENT
  # token: server-side only, never exposed to a browser.
  featureFlags:
    unleashUrl: "http://fuzefront-unleash.fuzefront.svc.cluster.local:4242/api"
    appName: "security-service"
    tokenSecretName: "unleash-secrets"
    tokenSecretKey: "UNLEASH_CLIENT_TOKEN"
  # Ingress NetworkPolicy allowing mendys-prod's datasets-service to reach
  # fuzefront-security in-cluster (FuzeFront#493 / FuzeInfra#339). Base
  # values.yaml default is OFF; enabling here is the deliberate deploy-window
  # step called out in FuzeInfra#501's fix — the policy was never actually
  # applied while Argo was stuck on the authentik-server-ingress port:0 bug.
  #
  # DEPLOY-WINDOW VERIFY after this syncs: from a mendys-prod pod,
  #   curl -sv --max-time 5 http://fuzefront-security.fuzefront.svc.cluster.local:3002/api/v1/security/session
  # should reach the service (not time out / connection-refused), and confirm
  # the existing Traefik + intra-fuzefront paths to fuzefront-security still work.
  networkPolicy:
    enabled: true
  # ── Second identity tenant: MendysRobotics (FuzeFront#434) ─────────────────
  # NOT YET ACTIVE. `tenants: []` (inherited from values.yaml) keeps
  # security-service in legacy single-tenant mode — the FuzeFront tenant's
  # behaviour is unchanged by this file. This block is the exact, ready-to-use
  # shape for the day it CAN go live; it is commented out rather than enabled
  # with placeholder secrets, because a tenant entry with a real clientId but
  # no real clientSecret/adminToken does not degrade gracefully — the pod
  # boots, then every Mendys login fails at the Authentik token exchange with
  # no signal until someone actually tries to sign in.
  #
  # Three things block flipping this on, none of which this repo can supply:
  #   1. FuzeInfra#421's authentik-mendys-server must be live and reachable at
  #      the in-cluster address below — CONFIRM the real Service name/
  #      namespace before copying this in; `authentik-mendys-server:9000`
  #      (bare, no .namespace suffix — mirroring how authentik-server:9000 is
  #      addressed above) is what the issue names, not yet independently
  #      verified against a running FuzeInfra manifest from this repo.
  #   2. An OIDC client + admin API token provisioned INSIDE that instance for
  #      this platform (mirroring the akadmin bootstrap token FuzeFront's own
  #      tenant reuses above), then sealed by the owner into the existing
  #      `fuzefront-secrets` SealedSecret (deploy/contabo/SEAL_PROD_SECRETS.md)
  #      under the three key names referenced below — `kubeseal` only, never
  #      plaintext in this file or in git.
  #   3. mendys-enrollment / mendys-login flow blueprints provisioned in that
  #      Authentik instance (mirrors flow-enrollment.yaml / flow-authentication.yaml
  #      for the FuzeFront tenant) — confirm the real slugs match what's below.
  #
  # Once all three are true: uncomment, fix any placeholder marked CONFIRM,
  # and also uncomment the matching `ingress.tenantIdentityHosts` entry below
  # — the two lists are independent and BOTH are required (see that value's
  # comment in values.yaml) or logins 400 despite the tenant being declared.
  #
  # tenants:
  #   - id: mendys
  #     hosts:
  #       - live.mendysrobotics.com
  #       - marketplace.mendysrobotics.com
  #     issuerUrl: https://live.mendysrobotics.com/application/o/mendys-platform/  # CONFIRM
  #     baseUrl: http://authentik-mendys-server:9000  # CONFIRM in-cluster address
  #     clientId: mendys-platform-oidc-client  # CONFIRM
  #     redirectUri: https://live.mendysrobotics.com/api/auth/oidc/callback
  #     adminTokenKey: AUTHENTIK_MENDYS_ADMIN_TOKEN        # seal into fuzefront-secrets
  #     clientSecretKey: AUTHENTIK_MENDYS_CLIENT_SECRET    # seal into fuzefront-secrets
  #     enrollmentFlowSlug: mendys-enrollment  # CONFIRM
  #     authFlowSlug: mendys-login             # CONFIRM (defaults to
  #       # default-authentication-flow if omitted — only correct if this
  #       # instance never got a dedicated combined-stage flow like
  #       # FuzeFront's fuzefront-auth)
  #     appBaseUrl: https://live.mendysrobotics.com
  #     # Per issue #434 scope item 5: this tenant's whole premise is that
  #     # Authentik is invisible to it, so the server-brokered Google path
  #     # must be on (never Authentik's /source/oauth/* browser redirect).
  #     googleBrokered: true
  #     # Per issue #434 scope item 5 ("a design question"): left UNSET here,
  #     # which falls back to the platform-wide GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET (see
  #     # tenants.ts). That means a Mendys user's Google consent screen shows
  #     # FuzeFront's app name/branding — acceptable only if the owner is fine
  #     # with that; if not, this tenant needs its OWN Google OAuth client,
  #     # declared as googleClientId + googleClientSecretKey (a third sealed
  #     # key: AUTHENTIK_MENDYS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET) here. Unresolved — see
  #     # the PR's open questions.

  # Social-broker return-origin allowlist (FuzeFront#352). MendysRobotics'
  # marketplace/live SPAs delegate sign-in entirely to this brokered social
  # flow and proxy /api/v1/security/* SAME-ORIGIN to fuzefront-security (see
  # the networkPolicy comment above — same mendys-prod integration, FuzeInfra
  # #339). Without this, the broker's success/error redirect always lands on
  # FRONTEND_URL (app.fuzefront.com) instead of the origin that started the
  # flow, so the mendys SPA never receives its `?code=`. EXACT origins only —
  # see providers/authentik/socialReturnOrigins.ts; this does NOT add either
  # host to `tenants` above (that would additionally require enumerating every
  # in-cluster caller's Host header or SECURITY_TENANTS' fail-closed rejection
  # breaks provisioning-service/config-service/selection-list-service too —
  # out of scope for this ask, see the module doc comment).
  socialReturnOrigins:
    - "https://marketplace.mendysrobotics.com"
    - "https://live.mendysrobotics.com"
  <<: *elasticPlacement

# FuzeFront's per-product A2A pod (owner decision: one pod per product, not a
# tenant row on the shared izzywdev/FuzeAgent `a2a-shared` server — see
# docs/a2a/README.md and FuzeAgent's docs/a2a/per-product-pod.md, transcribed
# here verbatim per that investigation's exact recipe). Runs the EXISTING
# shared ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzeagent-a2a image; this repo builds nothing new.
#
# Image is pinned by digest (see the `image.tag` comment below) — verified
# anonymously pullable 2026-08-23. Re-pin when FuzeAgent's CI publishes a new
# build.
#
# The A2A pod uses the shared FuzeInfra LiteLLM gateway. Its credential is the
# existing FuzeFront `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` entry, so no raw Anthropic key is
# duplicated into this namespace. The independent card-signing key remains a
# required SealedSecret and is generated by rotate-sealed-secret.yml.
#
# `a2a-repos-git` is NOT needed: FuzeFront is a PUBLIC repo (verified via the
# GitHub API), so the repo-sync init container clones anonymously.
# `ghcr-pull` is NOT needed either: ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuze-a2a is a public
# GHCR package (verified — anonymous token exchange + manifest GET succeeded).
a2a:
  enabled: true
  image:
    # CORRECTED 2026-09-02: ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzeagent-a2a (this pin's prior
    # value) is a stale/abandoned image — last pushed 2026-08-24, still
    # anonymously pullable but no longer built by anything. FuzeAgent's own
    # release.yml ("Build & push a2a-shared" step) builds
    # agent-templates/a2a/Dockerfile — the ONE shared A2A runtime — and
    # publishes it ONLY as ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuze-a2a:{sha,latest}; that is
    # also what FuzeAgent's own deploy/helm/a2a-shared/values-prod.yaml points
    # at. (gate-a2a's own I1 default + the runtime standard doc still name
    # `fuzeagent-a2a`; that is already-flagged gate/doc staleness, FuzeAgent
    # PR #257 — an I1 finding against this file is that, not a new fork.)
    repository: ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuze-a2a
    # Plain CI-built SHA tag. Verified anonymously pullable 2026-09-09
    # (anonymous GHCR token + manifest GET → HTTP 200 with OCI image index
    # media type). Re-pin when FuzeAgent's CI publishes a new build.
    # Previous tag `624956d8983b` returned HTTP 404 from GHCR on 2026-09-09
    # (likely purged from the registry on a retention policy); replaced with
    # the most recent tag that resolves clean.
    tag: "98b9b314bb0d"
    pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  service:
    type: ClusterIP
    port: 8080
  protocolVersion: "1.0"
  # MUST equal what the a2a-fuzefront Service resolves to (a2a.yaml). Unset

  # unreachable through its own signed card despite passing every probe.

    # `iss = https://app.fuzefront.com/application/o/` (no per-app slug); the

    #   python3 -c 'import sys,base64,json;p=sys.argv[1].split(".")[1];print(json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(p+"=="*(-len(p)%4)))["iss"])' "$TOK"
    # Set this field to exactly that string (host + trailing slash as emitted).
    oidcIssuerUrl: https://app.fuzefront.com/application/o/
    # In-cluster discovery avoids the Cloudflare-tunnel hairpin (17-34s

    # Unchanged: this URL is only the JWKS *locator* (its discovery doc yields

    oidcDiscoveryUrl: http://authentik-server.fuzefront.svc.cluster.local:9000/application/o/fuzefront/.well-known/openid-configuration

    callerClaim: repo

    keyId: a2a-v1

--- .github/workflows/release.yml ---
name: Release (images + GitOps bump)

# On merge to master that touches the platform: build backend/frontend, push to
# GHCR tagged with the commit SHA, then bump the tags in values-prod.yaml and
# commit. Argo CD sees the git change and rolls out the new images.
on:
  # Manual trigger: auto-merged PRs push to master under GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub
  # does NOT start push-triggered workflows for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes — so this
  # workflow otherwise never runs after an auto-merge and images never build.
  # Dispatch this after a deploy-window merge to build + bump the image tags.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      reason:
        description: 'Why this manual build (e.g. deploy security-service after an auto-merged PR)'
        required: false
        default: 'manual release'
  push:
    branches: [master]
    paths:
      # GENERATED BLOCK — do not hand-edit. Source of truth: deploy/deployable-paths.json.
      # Change it there, run `npm run deployable-paths:write`, commit both.
      # gate-deployable-paths.yml fails if these two disagree, because the failure mode of a
      # missing path is silent: the release workflow simply does not run, so the change merges
      # green and never ships. There is no red run to notice — there is no run.
      - 'backend/**'
      - 'shared/**'
      - 'frontend/**'
      # Workspace packages are COMPILED INTO the images (the backend/applications
      # images build @fuzefront/feature-flags; the frontend bundles the UI
      # packages from source via vite aliases). Without this, a change confined
      # to packages/** merges green and ships nothing — the images keep the old
      # code, which is exactly how a "merged" fix can fail to reach production.
      - 'packages/**'
      # api-client/ and sdk/ became root workspaces so packages-publish.yml
      # could see them at all, and the four root-installing Dockerfiles now COPY
      # their manifests (check-dockerfile-lockfile requires the full workspace
      # set, or npm hoists a different tree than the lockfile). That makes them
      # image inputs, so a change confined to either must rebuild.
      - 'api-client/**'
      - 'sdk/**'
      - 'services/email-service/**'
      - 'services/sms-service/**'
      - 'services/provisioning-service/**'
      - 'services/billing-service/**'
      # Added in the same change that discovered the gap: #432 added the
      # "Build & push chat-service" step below, but never added chat-service's
      # own path here, so a change confined to services/chat-service/** (not
      # touching packages/**, deploy/helm/fuzefront/**, or this file) would
      # merge green and NEVER trigger a release — the exact same silent-ship
      # failure mode the packages/** comment above describes, just for a
      # different path. This was live for every commit between #432 and now.
      - 'services/chat-service/**'
      # notification-service/** and payment-service/** were both missing here,
      # the same silent-ship gap the chat-service comment above describes: a
      # change confined to one of those service dirs would merge green and never
      # trigger a release, so the image would keep the old code (or, for the
      # never-built payment-service, stay absent entirely).
      - 'services/notification-service/**'
      - 'services/payment-service/**'
      - 'services/selection-list-service/**'
      - 'services/config-service/**'
      # docs/planning/developers-portal.md — devportal-service's own Dockerfile
      # also COPYs scripts/collect-devportal-specs.mjs and every services/*/openapi.yaml
      # it bundles (see that Dockerfile's `specs` build stage), so a change confined to
      # this dir alone still needs the SAME silent-ship protection every other service
      # path above exists for.
      - 'services/devportal-service/**'
      # Top-level, sibling to fuzefront-website/ — same self-contained-Dockerfile shape,
      # same silent-ship gap if this path were absent.
      - 'devportal-frontend/**'
      # Consumed by services/devportal-service/Dockerfile's `specs` build stage. A change
      # here changes what devportal-service bakes in without touching services/devportal-service/**
      # itself.
      - 'scripts/collect-devportal-specs.mjs'
      - 'clock-app/**'
      # fuzefront-website/frontend and fuzefront-website/backend each have their own
      # self-contained Dockerfile and are built into separate GHCR images. Without this
      # path a change confined to the public website would merge green and never ship.
      - 'fuzefront-website/**'
      - 'deploy/helm/fuzefront/**'
      - '.github/workflows/release.yml'

concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build-and-bump:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # commit the tag bump
      packages: write # push to GHCR
      actions: write # dispatch prod-post-deploy.yml (see the final step)
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@37fe631027851001ddb9b187196cc803df7f5f0e # v4.3.0

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@c94ce9fb468520275223c153574b00df6fe4bcc9 # v3.7.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Compute image tag
        id: tag
        run: echo "sha=${GITHUB_SHA::12}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build & push backend
        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: backend/Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: |
            ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-backend:${{ steps.tag.outputs.sha }}
            ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-backend:latest
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

      - name: Build & push frontend
        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: frontend/Dockerfile
          push: true
          build-args: |
            # Empty => the frontend uses window.location.origin (same-origin /api).
            # Robust across hosts: works on app.prod.fuzefront.com now and on
            # app.fuzefront.com after the 301 fast-follow, with no cross-origin/mixed
            # -content risk under the Cloudflare TLS edge. (api.ts: VITE_API_URL || origin)
            VITE_API_URL=
          tags: |
            ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-frontend:${{ steps.tag.outputs.sha }}
            ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-frontend:latest
          # Dedicated scope: the frontend build context changed from ./frontend to
          # repo root, so the old shared gha cache snapshot (where nginx.conf sat at
          # the context root, not frontend/) no longer matches and buildkit errors
          # with "frontend/nginx.conf: not found". A fresh scope busts that.
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=frontend-root
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=frontend-root

      - name: Build and push email-service
        id: email_image
        # Ancillary services are disabled in prod (only billing is enabled). They
        # must NEVER block the core backend+frontend deploy — a failed build here
        # is non-fatal; the bump+deploy still proceeds.
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: services/email-service/Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: |
            ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-email-service:${{ steps.tag.outputs.sha }}
            ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-email-service:latest
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

      - name: Build and push sms-service
        id: sms_image

        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: services/sms-service/Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: |
            ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-sms-service:${{ steps.tag.outputs.sha }}
            ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-sms-service:latest
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

      - name: Build and push provisioning-service
        id: provisioning_image
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: services/provisioning-service/Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: |
            ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-provisioning-service:${{ steps.tag.outputs.sha }}
            ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzefront-provisioning-service:latest

      - name: Build and push billing-service
        id: billing_image
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:

      - name: Build & push payment-service

        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .

        # Root build context: the Dockerfile runs `npm ci --workspace=

        id: notification_image

<!DOCTYPE html>

<style>
  * { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; }
  :root {
    --green: #008060;
    --green-dark: #004c3f;
    --green-light: #f0fdf7;
    --ink: #111827;
    --muted: #6b7280;
    --border: #e5e7eb;
    --bg: #f3f4f6;
  }
  html, body {
    font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;
    background: var(--bg);
    color: var(--ink);
    overscroll-behavior-y: none;
  }
  body {
    max-width: 520px;
    margin: 0 auto;
    min-height: 100vh;
    min-height: 100dvh;
    position: relative;
  }
  button { font-family: inherit; cursor: pointer; }
  input, textarea { font-family: inherit; }

  /* Header */
  .header {
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--green-dark) 0%, var(--green) 100%);
    padding: calc(20px + env(safe-area-inset-top)) 20px 30px;
    position: relative;
    overflow: hidden;
  }
  .header::before {
    content: ""; position: absolute; top: -30px; left: -30px; pointer-events: none;
    width: 140px; height: 140px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.05); border-radius: 50%;
  }
  .header::after {
    content: ""; position: absolute; bottom: -40px; right: -10px; pointer-events: none;
    width: 100px; height: 100px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.04); border-radius: 50%;
  }
  .header-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; position: relative; }
  .brand { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; }
  .brand-icon {
    background: rgba(255,255,255,0.15); border-radius: 10px; width: 38px; height: 38px;
    display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 20px;
  }
  .brand h1 { color: #fff; font-size: 20px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.5px; }
  .brand p { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.7); font-size: 12px; margin-top: 2px; }
  .gear {
    background: rgba(255,255,255,0.15); border: none; border-radius: 10px;
    width: 38px; height: 38px; color: #fff; font-size: 18px;
    display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; flex-shrink: 0;
  }

  /* Body */
  .body { padding: 16px 16px 40px; }

  /* Search */
  .search {
    background: #fff; border-radius: 14px; padding: 5px; display: flex; gap: 5px;
    box-shadow: 0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.1); margin-top: -18px; position: relative;
  }
  .search input {
    flex: 1; border: none; outline: none; padding: 12px 14px; font-size: 16px;
    background: transparent; color: var(--ink);
  }
  .search button {
    background: var(--green); color: #fff; border: none; border-radius: 10px;
    padding: 0 18px; font-weight: 700; font-size: 20px; min-width: 48px;
    display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; transition: background .15s;
  }
  .search button:disabled { background: #cbd5e1; }
  .search button:active:not(:disabled) { background: var(--green-dark); }
  html[dir="ltr"] .search button .arrow { transform: scaleX(-1); }

  /* Examples */
  .examples { margin-top: 16px; }
  .examples .label { font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); margin: 0 2px 8px; font-weight: 600; }
  .chips { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 7px; }
  .chip {
    background: #fff; border: 1.5px solid var(--border); border-radius: 20px;
    padding: 7px 13px; font-size: 13px; color: #374151;
  }
  .chip:active { background: var(--green-light); border-color: var(--green); }

  /* Loading */
  .loading { text-align: center; padding: 48px 20px; }
  .spinner {
    width: 44px; height: 44px; border: 3px solid var(--border); border-top-color: var(--green);
    border-radius: 50%; margin: 0 auto 14px; animation: spin .8s linear infinite;
  }
  @keyframes spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } }
  .loading p { color: var(--muted); font-size: 14px; }

  /* Empty */
  .empty { text-align: center; padding: 40px 24px; color: #9ca3af; }
  .empty .big { font-size: 52px; margin-bottom: 14px; }
  .empty .t { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; color: #6b7280; margin-bottom: 6px; }
  .empty .s { font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5; }

  /* Results */
  .result-title {
    background: #fff; border-radius: 14px; padding: 14px 16px; margin-bottom: 10px;
    box-shadow: 0 1px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.06); display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px;
    animation: fadeIn .3s ease;
  }
  .result-title .ico { background: var(--green-light); border-radius: 9px; padding: 9px; font-size: 18px; }
  .result-title .tag { font-size: 11px; color: var(--green); font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: 2px; }
  .result-title .txt { font-size: 17px; font-weight: 700; }

  .step {
    background: #fff; border-radius: 12px; padding: 13px 14px 10px; margin-bottom: 7px;
    box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.05); animation: fadeIn .3s ease backwards;
  }
  .step-main { display: flex; gap: 12px; align-items: flex-start; }
  .step .num {
    background: var(--green); color: #fff; border-radius: 50%; width: 28px; height: 28px;
    display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px;
    flex-shrink: 0; margin-top: 1px;
  }
  .step .action { font-weight: 600; font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.45; }
  .step .where { font-size: 12px; color: var(--green); margin-top: 4px; font-weight: 500; }
  .step .detail { font-size: 13px; color: #555; margin-top: 5px; line-height: 1.55; }
  .stuck-btn {
    margin: 8px 0 0 40px; background: none; border: none; color: #9ca3af;
    font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; padding: 4px 0; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px;
  }
  .stuck-btn:active { color: var(--green); }

  .callout {
    border-radius: 12px; padding: 13px 15px; margin-bottom: 8px; animation: fadeIn .3s ease;
  }
  .callout.tip { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #f0fdf7, #e8f9f3); border: 1px solid #a7f3d0; }
  .callout.shortcut { background: #fafafa; border: 1px solid var(--border); }
  .callout .ch { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: 5px; }
  .callout.tip .ch { color: var(--green); }
  .callout.shortcut .ch { color: var(--muted); }
  .callout .cb { font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.55; color: #1a1a1a; }

  .again {
    width: 100%; background: #fff; border: 2px solid var(--green); border-radius: 12px;
    padding: 13px; color: var(--green); font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; margin-top: 8px;
  }
  .again:active { background: var(--green-light); }

  .err {
    background: #fef2f2; border: 1px solid #fecaca; border-radius: 12px;
    padding: 14px; color: #dc2626; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5;
  }
  .cached-badge {
    display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; background: #eef2ff; color: #4f46e5;
    padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 10px; margin: 0 8px; font-weight: 600; vertical-align: middle;
  }
  .scope-note {
    background: #fffbeb; border: 1px solid #fde68a; border-radius: 12px;
    padding: 12px 14px; margin-bottom: 10px; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.55; color: #92400e;
    animation: fadeIn .3s ease;
  }

  @keyframes fadeIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(6px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }

  /* Bottom sheet (settings + stuck + wizard) */
  .overlay {
    position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.5); display: flex;
    align-items: flex-end; justify-content: center; z-index: 100; animation: fadeIn .2s;
  }
  .sheet {
    background: #fff; width: 100%; max-width: 520px; border-radius: 20px 20px 0 0;
    padding: 22px 20px calc(20px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom));
    animation: slideUp .28s ease; max-height: 92vh; max-height: 92dvh;
    display: flex; flex-direction: column;
  }
  @keyframes slideUp { from { transform: translateY(100%); } to { transform: none; } }
  .sheet h2 { font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: 6px; }
  .sheet .desc { font-size: 13px; color: var(--muted); line-height: 1.55; margin-bottom: 16px; }
  .sheet label { display: block; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; color: #374151; margin-bottom: 6px; }
  .sheet input[type=password], .sheet input[type=text] {
    width: 100%; border: 1.5px solid var(--border); border-radius: 10px; padding: 12px 14px;
    font-size: 15px; outline: none; direction: ltr; text-align: left;
  }
  .sheet input:focus, .sheet textarea:focus { border-color: var(--green); }
  .sheet .hint { font-size: 11px; color: #9ca3af; margin-top: 6px; line-height: 1.5; }
  .sheet .hint a { color: var(--green); }
  .sheet-scroll { overflow-y: auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; margin: 0 -4px; padding: 0 4px; }
  .settings-section { margin-top: 20px; padding-top: 18px; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
  .settings-section > label:first-child { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink); }
  .sheet-actions { display: flex; gap: 10px; margin-top: 18px; }
  .btn-primary {
    flex: 1; background: var(--green); color: #fff; border: none; border-radius: 11px;
    padding: 13px; font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px;
  }
  .btn-primary:active { background: var(--green-dark); }
  .btn-primary:disabled { background: #cbd5e1; }
  .btn-ghost {
    background: #fff; color: var(--muted); border: 1.5px solid var(--border); border-radius: 11px;
